g.text: Rendered evidence from captured output
required and optional saved-server attachments without round-tripping the whole config. Composed server-side from the client's cur
rent config, so every other setting is preserved — and `expectedConfigId` is required so two concurrent server replacements cannot
silently lose one…\n- [Duplicate a client](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/clients/duplicate-a-client.md): Creates a new cl
ient carrying the selected client's current config, and responds `201` with the copy's detail. Purely additive — the source is unt
ouched.\n- [Validate a server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-diagnostics/validate-a-server.md): Connects to the ser
ver, initializes the MCP session, and returns a connection snapshot (server info, negotiated capabilities). The same check the hos
ted inspector runs when you connect a server.\n- [Run the doctor](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-diagnostics/run-the
-doctor.md): Runs the full doctor workflow — probe → connect → initialize → capabilities → primitives — and returns a step-by-step
report. The richest signal for \"is this server healthy, and why not.\"\n- [Check OAuth requirement](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-
reference/server-diagnostics/check-oauth-requirement.md): Lightweight, no MCP connection: reports whether the server is configured
to require an OAuth grant.\n- [List tools](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-tools.md): Returns the server's
tools as a collection page. Each item is the MCP tool definition (`name`, `description`, `inputSchema`, ...).\n- [List prompts](ht
tps://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-prompts.md): Returns the server's prompts as a collection page.\n- [List resou
rces](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-resources.md): Returns the server's resources as a collection page.\n-
[Read a resource](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/read-a-resource.md): Reads a single resource by URI and return
s its contents.\n- [List server skills](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-server-skills.md): Returns the Agent
Skills a connected server serves over the MCP skills extension (SEP-2640), including skills it advertises that MCPJam declines to
load. Not paginated: the catalog is drained server-side, because duplicate detection spans the whole listing.\n- [Get a server sk
ill](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/get-a-server-skill.md): Fetches one skill by URI and verifies it before retu
rning a byte: the SKILL.md digest against the manifest, the fetched frontmatter against what the listing advertised, and the name
against the URI. Reaches skills a partial listing never mentioned. When a check fails the response carries a `refusal`…\n- [Read a
server skill's supporting file](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/read-a-server-skills-supporting-file.md): Reads
one supporting file belonging to a skill, checking its byte length and digest against the skill's own manifest. The manifest is th
e read allowlist and is re-fetched here rather than accepted from the caller, so a request cannot authorize its own read.\n- [Expo
rt a server snapshot](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/export/export-a-server-snapshot.md): Lists tools, resources, and promp
ts in one call and returns a single JSON snapshot — handy for diffing a server's surface over time in CI.\n- [Call a tool](https:/
/docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/call-a-tool.md): Executes a tool on the server and returns the MCP `CallToolResult` plus
an additive `durationMs` (wall-clock time of `executeTool`). Tool-level failures (`isError: true` in the result) are **successful
calls** — the server answered; only transport/auth errors use the error envelope.\n- [Render a prompt](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api
-reference/execution/render-a-prompt.md): Renders a prompt with arguments and returns the MCP `GetPromptResult` directly (`descrip
tion?`, `messages`).\n- [Render an MCP App widget headlessly](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/render-an-mcp-app-wi
dget-headlessly.md): Call an MCP App tool and mount its `ui://` widget in real headless Chromium running the production host bridg
e, then report whether it rendered, what it logged, what it was blocked from fetching, and the widget as an accessibility tree wit
h addressable elements.\n- [Create a retained widget session](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/create-a-retained-wi
dget-session.md): Available only on the local Inspector that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verifi
ed user or API key. A session is bound to the original subject, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Executes th
e tool and retains its App in one local Chromium context.…\n- [Read a retained widget snapshot](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-refere
nce/execution/read-a-retained-widget-snapshot.md): Available only on the local Inspector that created the session; hosted deployme
nts return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to the original subject, project and server and expires af
ter its idle timeout. Returns an accessibility tree and addressable elements without replay…\n- [Act on a retained widget](https:/
/docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/act-on-a-retained-widget.md): Available only on the local Inspector that created the sess
ion; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to the original subject, project and s
erver and expires after its idle timeout. Runs one coordinate action with fresh project/server authorization.\n- [Run a retained w
idget step](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/run-a-retained-widget-step.md): Available only on the local Inspector
that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to the original s
ubject, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Runs one semantic action or assertion, using the same locator vocab
ul…\n- [Close a retained widget session](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/close-a-retained-widget-session.md): Avai
lable only on the local Inspector that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A
session is bound to the original subject, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Disposes the original owner's bro
wser. Returns closed=false if no mat…\n- [List a suite's settings history](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-suites/list-
a-suites-settings-history.md): One entry per committed edit to the suite's settings, newest first: who made it, which STORED field
s moved, the note they left, how many runs were launched against it, and the revision group that ties one request's writes togethe
r. Rows carry no configuration snapshots. Send a `revisionNumber` back…\n- [Attach one environment to a suite (atomic append)](htt
ps://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-suites/attach-one-environment-to-a-suite-atomic-append.md): APPEND one project environment
to the suite's attachments, if it is not already there.\n- [List a server's accounts](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/serve
r-accounts/list-a-servers-accounts.md): The accounts this server signs in with that you can see: your own personal accounts, or, o
n a server shared with the project, its project accounts. Another member's personal account never appears. METADATA ONLY: no accou
nt response carries a token.\n- [Get a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/get-a-server-account.
md): One account, by id or name. Another member's personal account answers `404`, the same as a missing one. A name two accounts s
hare answers `409` with `details.code: \"account_name_ambiguous\"` and both ids in `details.accountIds`.\n- [Upload tokens to a se
rver account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/upload-tokens-to-a-server-account.md): Creates the account (`2
01`) or replaces its token in place (`200`, same id). A well-formed account id never creates one: an unknown id is `404`. Any othe
r reference is a name, and a name no account has creates the account.\n- [Delete a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-ref
erence/server-accounts/delete-a-server-account.md): Deletes the account and its stored token. The token's issuer is asked to revok
e it where the issuer supports revocation (best effort), which also invalidates any copy of the same token you hold.\n- [Rename a
